messages.text:
"The core concept is a hardcore open-world 3D vehicle mechanic and survival simulator. The gameplay loop seamlessly blends high-fidelity mechanical assembly with punishing first-person life simulation.
The player starts in a remote rural area with a completely bare car chassis and a garage full of loose individual parts like pistons, crankshafts, and wiring looms. Every component must be manually installed and fastened using specific tool sizes, where loose bolts lead to mechanical failure and overtightening strips the threads. Beyond assembly, the player must finely tune the engine, including carburetor fuel-air mixtures, valve clearances, and wheel alignment, while parts realistically wear down or catastrophically fail under stress.
To fund this project, the player navigates the open world using secondary vehicles like tractors, mopeds, or trucks to perform odd jobs for local residents, such as hauling firewood or clearing septic tanks. Survival mechanics run parallel to the mechanical simulation, requiring the player to manage shifting meters for hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, and hygiene, where failure or severe driving accidents result in permadeath. The game features no active hand-holding or guidance, immersing the player in a gritty, high-stakes sandbox of automotive grease, financial struggle, and raw mechanical trial-and-error
"

### Concept / narrative
Title: **BARE METAL**
Tagline: "No manual. No mercy."
Setting: Hollow Creek, late autumn. You inherit a dead garage and a stripped 1974 pickup. You have $40, a moped, and a body that needs feeding.

Opening: title screen shows garage at dusk from a low cinematic angle, dust, warm bulb, chassis. Text and start.

When start: first-person in garage, brief diegetic note on bench: "Truck: 4.6L straight-six. Service book in the office. — Dad". Objective implicit: build truck, earn money, survive.

### HUD
Bottom left: five meters as vertical bars or horizontal thin lines: HUNGER, THIRST, FATIGUE, STRESS, HYGIENE. Icons plus percent. Keep small. Top right money and time/day. Top left location "HOLLOW CREEK / GARAGE". Center reticle dot. Interaction prompt near center bottom: "[E] Install carburetor" or "[HOLD LMB] Torque 12mm bolt". Context hints.

No quest markers except diegetic notes and a clipboard on bench listing jobs. Jobs available via a board in garage: "FIREWOOD — Miller farm — $120", etc. Clicking board opens job list, accept, then drive.

Tool selection: number keys 1-5 or mouse wheel; visible as a bottom-center tool belt with icons/names. Mobile: tap tool belt.

### Mechanics

**Player movement (FPS):** pointer lock on click. WASD, shift sprint, crouch C, E interact. Head bob. Collision with garage walls/shelves simplified AABB. Move speed 3.2. On mobile, left virtual joystick + drag look + E button.

4. Carburetor — bench. 10mm, 2 bolts.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable browser-game vertical slice from the user’s pitch: a hardcore open-world 3D vehicle-mechanic and survival simulator with manual part assembly, bolt torque tolerances, engine tuning, odd jobs, driving, survival meters, and permadeath.

## Requirements
- No explicit deliverable format was stated by the user beyond the game concept.
- Preserve hardcore/no-hand-holding tone: diegetic manual, permadeath, no active quest hand-holding.
- Core loop to demonstrate: bare chassis + loose parts → torque assembly → fluids → tune mixture/timing/valve clearance → start truck → drive jobs → earn money → manage hunger/thirst/fatigue/stress/hygiene.
- Include secondary vehicle (moped), first-person movement, rural open world, garage, farm/store destinations.
- Mobile support expected from project conventions: responsive layout and touch controls.

## Decisions
- Built original Three.js + Vite game titled **BARE METAL — A Rustbelt Survival Sim**, packaged as a static web build.
- Vertical slice scope: one garage, one 1974 pickup (“The Patient”), six installable part groups (battery, carb, alternator, radiator, spark plugs, wheels), 16 torque steps, three tune settings, two jobs (courier $35, firewood $150), moped and truck driving, survival meters and permadeath.
- All art/audio is procedural: canvas textures, procedural Three.js geometry, WebAudio synthesis, locally bundled Google fonts.
- UI aesthetic: oil-black/cream/rust, Barlow Condensed + IBM Plex Mono + Special Elite, paper manual/job board, dark diagnostic console, analog torque gauge.
- Debug hook exposed as `window.BareMetal = { game, world, ui, input, sound, mode, enterVehicle, exitVehicle, startTorque }`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` (three ^0.187, vite ^7.3.7), Vite build passes (`npm run build`).
- Full 3D world: garage with walls/roof/trusses/lights/windows, truck on jack stands, moped, workbench, shelves, cot, sink, desk/terminal, job board, stove, parts/crates, outdoor road, farm, store, fences, power lines, trees, hills, dust/exhaust particles.
- Truck and moped models, part visibility, wheels, cargo logs, bolt visuals.
- Game state/save/permadeath, survival tick, fluid/food/coffee/smoke/sleep actions, store purchases, jobs, tuning math, engine-start outcome.
- FPS controls, collision, interactions/raycasting, hold-to-load jobs, truck/moped driving physics, chase camera, crash damage.
- UI: start screen, HUD, survival bars, toolbelt, prompts, manual, job board, store terminal, tuning panel, torque gauge canvas, pause/death screens, mobile joystick/action button markup.
- Procedural sound: ambient wind, footsteps, ratchet/tool sounds, engine/moped loops, radio, crash/UI sounds.
- WebAudio, font loading, and Vite production build verified with no JS console errors after latest fix.
- Title screen scene now renders correctly after fixing opaque start background and auto-adding world meshes to the scene.
- Latest fix moved mount hint sprites into `buildTruck()`, resolving `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'group')`.
- Latest title screenshot (`screenshots/title5.png`) shows correct UI but the 3D background is a close-up rusty wall, not the intended truck/garage composition.

### Active
- Visual framing/lighting polish of title and first-person views.
- Functional playtesting of the full assembly → tuning → driving → job loop.
- Mobile layout/testing not yet done.

### Blocked
- Title camera now appears to be inside/too close to the truck or wall after last camera edit; needs correction in `updateTitle()`.

## Next Move
1. Fix `updateTitle()` camera to a clean garage/truck composition (previous good framing was around `position (4.55, 2.05, 4.75)`, `lookAt (0.2, 1.22, -0.7)`; current `(5.25, 2.35, 6.15)` looks wrong/occluded).
2. Reload and capture title + gameplay screenshots; verify truck, tools, parts, and HUD readability.
3. Playtest interactions via Playwright/BareMetal debug hook: pick up parts, install at correct tool sizes, torque with the gauge, fill fluids, tune to manual specs, start engine.
4. Verify driving to Miller farm/store, job load/unload, payout, truck cargo logs, fuel use, exit vehicle.
5. Verify manual, board, store, tuning overlays and pause/death restart flow.
6. Test desktop and 390×844 mobile layout; fix touch controls and safe-area overlap.
7. Remove or guard any debug artifacts and ensure final `npm run build` + capture succeeds.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: renderer, loop, modes, player/drive controllers, interaction routing, title camera, debug hook.
- `src/world.js`: full environment, interactables, colliders, particles, markers, mount hints, lighting.
- `src/truck.js`: pickup/moped models, `PART_INFO` (tools/torque), part visibility, bolt meshes.
- `src/game.js`: state, save/load, survival, tuning, engine start, jobs, store, death.
- `src/ui.js`: all DOM UI, HUD, panels, torque gauge, death/pause.
- `src/style.css`: full visual design, responsive/mobile rules.
- `src/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/pointer-lock/touch input.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio.
- `src/tex.js`: procedural canvas textures.
- `index.html`: app structure and panels.
- `screenshots/title5.png`: latest title screenshot; `screenshots/play2.png`: latest gameplay screenshot.
- `src/fonts/`: bundled woff2 fonts (barlow, IBM Plex Mono, Special Elite).

## Important Context
- Dev server runs in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002` via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`; Vite build watch is active.
- Use `playwright-cli` with `DISPLAY=:0`; browser installed under `~/.cache/ms-playwright`. Reload command: `playwright-cli reload`; start via `playwright-cli click "#startBtn"` (text selector fails).
- `capture.sh` auto-starts by clicking a visible button whose label exactly matches `Start`/`Start Game`/`Play`/`Play Now`; current button is `Start Game`.
- Screenshot viewport set to 1440×900 via `playwright-cli resize 1440 900`.
- World helpers `box`/`cyl`/`plane` now auto-add to `defaultScene` when no parent is passed; this fixed missing garage geometry.
- Save key: `baremetal.v1`; Start loads existing save; death wipes it and restart uses `location.reload()`.
- Three.js warnings only: `THREE.Clock` deprecated and `PCFSoftShadowMap` removed (falls back to PCFShadowMap). No runtime JS errors after the mount-hint fix.
- Latest title screenshot shows UI fine but background is a close rusty wall—likely title camera position/orientation or occlusion by truck/wall; inspect `updateTitle()` in `src/main.js`.
- In-game survival meter fills were faint in screenshots; CSS was updated to brighter `#d9c9a8` fills and a dark HUD gradient, not re-verified since.
- Truck hood underside was previously a large rusty slab; it was changed to a dark ribbed underside, more upright (`-1.24`), and a prop rod/jack stands were added—not yet visually verified.

messages.text:
"The core concept is a hardcore open-world 3D vehicle mechanic and survival simulator. The gameplay loop seamlessly blends high-fidelity mechanical assembly with punishing first-person life simulation.
The player starts in a remote rural area with a completely bare car chassis and a garage full of loose individual parts like pistons, crankshafts, and wiring looms. Every component must be manually installed and fastened using specific tool sizes, where loose bolts lead to mechanical failure and overtightening strips the threads. Beyond assembly, the player must finely tune the engine, including carburetor fuel-air mixtures, valve clearances, and wheel alignment, while parts realistically wear down or catastrophically fail under stress.
To fund this project, the player navigates the open world using secondary vehicles like tractors, mopeds, or trucks to perform odd jobs for local residents, such as hauling firewood or clearing septic tanks. Survival mechanics run parallel to the mechanical simulation, requiring the player to manage shifting meters for hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, and hygiene, where failure or severe driving accidents result in permadeath. The game features no active hand-holding or guidance, immersing the player in a gritty, high-stakes sandbox of automotive grease, financial struggle, and raw mechanical trial-and-error
